overview.rule: Lair listings are provided for monsters described as having lairs.
Each lair is unique and should appear only once in the campaign.

uses.use: Dynamic points of interest discovered during wilderness travel.
Obstacles that must be addressed when securing land for a domain.

definitions.definition: A pre-placed settlement, dungeon, or other locale with a fixed location on the regional map from the start of play.
A monster lair from wilderness encounter tables whose location is not fixed until first encountered in lair.

regional_map_guidance.rule: A typical regional map of 40 x 30 6-mile hexes is recommended to contain 45 static points of interest.
Dynamic points of interest reduce the need to pre-stock all empty hexes.

placement_procedure.step: When a wilderness encounter throw results in an encounter with a monster in its lair, place that monster's dynamic point of interest in the hex where the encounter occurred.
Once placed, the point of interest becomes static and remains fixed in that hex for the rest of the campaign.
Record the hex number on the regional map for later return.

hex_definition.rule: A 6-mile hex covers 31 square miles, about 24,000 acres.
A hex can support many peasants when settled and farmed.
Before peasants can settle a hex, the hex must be cleared of monster lairs present within it, subject to Judge discretion on whether undiscovered lairs actually prevent secure settlement.

lair_generation_procedure.step: Cross-reference terrain type and hex classification on the lairs_per_hex table and roll to determine the number of lairs present.
Treat any result less than 0 as 0.
If the table entry is "-", no random lairs are present.
For each lair indicated, roll on the appropriate column of the Wilderness Encounters by Terrain table to determine the monster type in the lair.
For each resulting monster, select a lair from the book's lair listings and place it within the hex.

density_guidance.rule: Most wilderness hexes will have three to six lairs.
More settled hexes will have fewer lairs.
Lairs are denser in terrain with many hiding places, such as jungles and swamps, and less dense in open terrain with long lines of sight.

core_rules.rule: A party must find a lair before it can clear it.
Searching for lairs in the wilderness functions like searching for traps in a dungeon in that a lair may exist without being found by a given search attempt.
Fast-moving parties are better at finding lairs than parties slowed by encumbrance or terrain.
If the Judge has a detailed small-scale map of the 6-mile hex, the Judge may adjudicate searching directly from that map instead of using the abstract search system.

abstract_search_procedure.step: For each hour of searching, equal to six turns, make one secret searching throw on behalf of the party using 1d20.
Determine the target value from the party's daily movement rate through the hex using the lair_search_target_values table.
If the die roll equals or exceeds the target value, the party discovers a lair if at least one lair is present.
If more than one lair is present, choose one or determine it randomly.

tracking.rule: If any party member has the Tracking proficiency, the party receives a +4 bonus on the lair search roll.
If the adjusted die roll equals or exceeds the listed target value, the party discovers one lair within the hex.

aerial_reconnaissance.rule: If the party is capable of air travel, double its daily wilderness movement rate.
When searching clear, grass, scrub, hills, barren, desert, or mountain terrain by air, the party receives one search throw every three turns, or thirty minutes, instead of one per hour.

wandering_monsters.rule: Adventurers searching a hex are subject to one wandering encounter throw per hour while searching.
Searching parties are more likely to encounter monsters than parties merely passing through quickly.

If the party accidentally wanders into a lair, substitute the newly encountered lair for one of the previously generated lairs, or substitute one of the previously generated lairs for the newly encountered lair.

splitting_up.rule: If the party splits into smaller sub-parties, each sub-party may make a separate searching throw.
Each sub-party is also subject to wandering encounters separately and must handle them on its own.
If sub-parties are close enough to assist each other in encounters, they are not meaningfully split and are effectively searching the same area.

assessment_rules.rule: A character with the Land Surveying proficiency may attempt to assess the total number of lairs in a hex based on terrain, evidence of cultivation, and similar factors.
The character may attempt one assessment on first arriving in the hex, and one additional assessment each time the hex is searched.

procedure.step: The Judge secretly rolls 1d20 on the character's behalf.
Apply a cumulative +4 bonus for each successful search the party has conducted in that hex up to that point.
On success, the character correctly assesses the number of lairs in the hex, and the Judge reveals that number.
If the throw fails with an unmodified 1, the character makes an incorrect assessment, and the Judge rolls or chooses a false number to reveal.
On any other failure, the character does not yet have enough information to make or revise an assessment.

limits.limit: Without definitive magic such as commune, a party can never be certain it has found all possible lairs in a hex.
A lair may remain undiscovered for weeks, years, or generations.

judge_guidance.rule: The Judge decides whether an undiscovered lair prevents the hex from being considered secured for settlement.
This judgment depends on how disruptive the undiscovered lair would be to settlement.

type.name: pathfinder
type.rule: Pathfinders are 1st level explorers with the Pathfinder template.
type.duty: Can be hired to search hexes for lairs.

type.name: land_surveyor
type.rule: Land surveyors are 1st level explorers with the Cartographer template.
type.duty: Can be hired to assess the number of lairs in a hex.

availability.rule: Both scout types are hired on a monthly basis.
They are available in urban settlements in the same numbers as navigators.

protection_requirements.rule: Scouts expect protection while on duty from their employer or from a number of mercenaries equal to the maximum number of lairs in the hex or hexes they are assigned to explore.

behavior.rule: Scouts attempt to evade wandering monsters.
They will not fight for their employer.
They will not enter lairs unless recruited as henchmen.

references.reference: Wilderness Encounters by Terrain table is required to determine lair monster types.
ACKS p. 94 is referenced for aerial movement doubling.
Player's Companion p. 66 is referenced for Pathfinder and Cartographer templates.
Commune is cited as an example of definitive magic that could confirm whether all lairs have been found.
